final_message:
The bug was in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`. When a customer had no default payment method, it returned `None` straight away. That skipped `record_failure`, so nothing counted the attempt, scheduled a retry, emitted `invoice.payment_failed`, or moved the subscription to `past_due`.

The fix is to call `record_failure(ctx, invoice, "no_payment_method")` before returning in that case. A missing payment method now follows the same dunning path as an expired card. The 24 existing tests pass, but I didn't add a test for the no-payment-method case.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root: `{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}`.

steps.command: ls billing && grep -n "payment_method\|def " billing/*.py | grep -i "payment_method\|dunning\|charge\|attempt" | head -50

python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    if method is None:\n        return None\n","    if method is None:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, \"no_payment_method\")\n        return None\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8
